To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the viva is a critical component of the doctoral process, that it is a private and confidential event, that it is an opportunity for the student to demonstrate their understanding of the research process, that it has a significant impact on the student, that students should prepare for the viva by reading widely and by rehearsing with their supervisors, and that the viva should be seen as an opportunity rather than a threat.
the viva is a critical part of the PhD experience, and that the process is a significant test for students, but that it is not always a fair one.

the viva vo ce is a critical component of the doctoral examination process and is the final hurdle in the doctoral process; that it is the responsibility of the internal examiner to guide the student through the process, and the external examiner’s role is to challenge; and that the process is not transparent and lacks accountability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the doctoral student can be best prepared to meet the challenges of the viva, and the implications of this for supervisors and the institution.
issues of fairness, equity and accountability, and with the question of whether, in the UK, the doctoral viva is a fair, equitable and rigorous examination process.
the viva as an important and final stage of the PhD process and with its role in the production of knowledge, the development of the doctoral candidate and the quality of the PhD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the viva vo ce process is not fit for purpose, but that is a matter for further debate.
the PhD viva is a process in search of a purpose.
the viva vo ce is a process that is in urgent need of reform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PhD viva is not only a critical part of the PhD journey, but also an opportunity for the student to demonstrate his/her understanding, knowledge, and critical analysis of the field.
we have found that the viva is a complex, multifaceted and often misunderstood process.
the viva is an important, but not necessarily the most important, part of the PhD process, and that it should be seen as a ‘celebration’ of achievement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PhD viva is a critical component of doctoral study and needs to be taken more seriously by all stakeholders.
students and supervisors need to be aware of the importance of preparing for the viva, and that the process is a two-way street.
the viva voxe should not be seen as a mysterious, frightening event, but as a process that can be prepared for and conducted in a way that is both fair and transparent.
